title: Trigonometric Ratios: Sine, Cosine and Tangent
seo_title: Trigonometric Ratios – SSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Use sine, cosine and tangent in right-angled triangles to find sides and angles; use the special angles 30°, 45° and 60°. (summary of the NERDC SSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 maths worksheets on trigonometric ratios: SOH CAH TOA, finding sides and angles, and the values for 30°, 45° and 60°. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: sin = opp/hyp, cos = adj/hyp, tan = opp/adj
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle; the opposite side faces the angle.
  • Choose the ratio that uses the side you know and the side you want.
  • sin 30° = 1/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 45° = 1.

Examples

Example

Hypotenuse 10 cm, angle 30°. Opposite?

10 × sin 30°

Answer: 5 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up the opposite and adjacent sidesFind the angle first, then label.
Using tan for the hypotenusetan does not use the hypotenuse.
Calculator in radiansSet it to degrees.

items.q: Which side is the adjacent, relative to the angle θ?
items.e: The adjacent side is next to θ (and is not the hypotenuse): A.

items.q: In a right-angled triangle, the opposite side is 6 cm and the adjacent side is 9 cm. Which ratio finds an angle?
items.e: SOH: sin = O/H. CAH: cos = A/H. TOA: tan = O/A. With the opposite side and adjacent side, use tan (TOA).

items.q: If sin A = 4/5, find sec A (A is acute).
items.e: Draw a right triangle with sin A = 4/5: the sides are opposite 4, adjacent 3, hypotenuse 5 (Pythagoras). So sec A = 5/3.

items.q: If sec A = 17/15, find cos A (A is acute).
items.e: Draw a right triangle with sec A = 17/15: the sides are opposite 8, adjacent 15, hypotenuse 17 (Pythagoras). So cos A = 15/17.

items.q: If cos A = 8/17, find cosec A (A is acute).
items.e: Draw a right triangle with cos A = 8/17: the sides are opposite 15, adjacent 8, hypotenuse 17 (Pythagoras). So cosec A = 17/15.

items.q: If cos A = 15/17, find sin A (A is acute).
items.e: Draw a right triangle with cos A = 15/17: the sides are opposite 8, adjacent 15, hypotenuse 17 (Pythagoras). So sin A = 8/17.

items.q: If cot A = 24/7, find sin A (A is acute).
items.e: Draw a right triangle with cot A = 24/7: the sides are opposite 7, adjacent 24, hypotenuse 25 (Pythagoras). So sin A = 7/25.

items.q: If cosec A = 37/12, find cos A (A is acute).
items.e: Draw a right triangle with cosec A = 37/12: the sides are opposite 12, adjacent 35, hypotenuse 37 (Pythagoras). So cos A = 35/37.

items.q: If cosec A = 13/5, find sin A (A is acute).
items.e: Draw a right triangle with cosec A = 13/5: the sides are opposite 5, adjacent 12, hypotenuse 13 (Pythagoras). So sin A = 5/13.

items.q: If sin A = 7/25, find cosec A (A is acute).
items.e: Draw a right triangle with sin A = 7/25: the sides are opposite 7, adjacent 24, hypotenuse 25 (Pythagoras). So cosec A = 25/7.

items.q: If sec A = 13/12, find cosec A (A is acute).
items.e: Draw a right triangle with sec A = 13/12: the sides are opposite 5, adjacent 12, hypotenuse 13 (Pythagoras). So cosec A = 13/5.

items.q: If sec A = 5/3, find cos A (A is acute).
items.e: Draw a right triangle with sec A = 5/3: the sides are opposite 4, adjacent 3, hypotenuse 5 (Pythagoras). So cos A = 3/5.
